source.title: Gaussian Universality of Linear Classifiers with Random Labels in High-Dimension
source.authors: Federica Gerace; Florent Krzakala; Bruno Loureiro; Ludovic Stephan; Lenka Zdeborov'a

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though its title differs slightly from the catalog title. It is not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: Tests training performance with random labels using generalized linear classifiers and fixed feature maps, rather than standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods.
record.gate_note: The paper studies random-label training loss for generalized linear classifiers, including fixed-feature models described as relevant to the lazy regime. It does not report test error, training time, shuffled or Gaussian-noise inputs, a sweep over corrupted-label fractions, regularization effects on random-label fitting versus true-label generalization, or learning order. Cited results from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures minimum convex training loss for perceptrons and fixed-feature classifiers, rather than random-label fitting by standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods. Its proposed connection to deep networks in the lazy regime does not supply results for the systems named in V1–V6. Gaussian universality is a related but different claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors prove asymptotic training-loss universality for homogeneous Gaussian mixtures under their stated loss assumptions; vanishing-regularization square loss permits heterogeneous mixtures. Real-dataset evidence is empirical. They argue relevance to deep networks in the lazy regime, while leaving broader multilayer-network and non-convex extensions for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes high-dimensional generalized linear classifiers and fixed feature maps, with convex optimization and asymptotic training-loss comparisons. It does not reproduce the original deep-network stochastic-gradient experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The universality result at finite regularization assumes homogeneous covariances across mixture components. The text reports small deviations for a deliberately heterogeneous Gaussian mixture; preprocessing is associated with greater similarity among real-data mode covariance matrices.

fits_no_version.finding: At vanishing regularization, empirical training-loss curves for fixed-feature classifiers on real datasets agree with Gaussian predictions. Theorem 5 gives square loss 0 for α ≤ 1 and (1 − 1/α)/2 for α > 1 in the stated Gaussian-mixture setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-dimensional perceptrons with independent random binary labels exhibit Gaussian universality of minimum training loss under stated assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite-regularization training losses on transformed tiny ImageNet agree with single-Gaussian predictions using corresponding covariances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gaussian predictions with matching covariance describe regularized fixed-feature classifier training losses on these real datasets.

record.problems: The numerical results are primarily plotted rather than tabulated. The experiments use finite datasets and fixed feature maps or generalized linear classifiers, and do not directly measure test error or compare training time with true labels.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numeric result rows were left out. The paper also reports finite-regularization curves and unprocessed-dataset curves in Figs. 2 and 5, plus heterogeneous-mixture comparisons in Fig. 3; those measure training loss under different regularization or data conditions but do not establish the fitting-error, time, test-error, or other version-specific outcomes. Exact plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks with stochastic gradient training, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test error.
Training-time comparison with true labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
The same deep networks fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Whether weight decay, dropout and augmentation prevent deep networks fitting random labels, and generalization after removing these regularizers.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise; no learning trajectories or real-label comparison are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The row states indicate inability to determine any listed version's effect, not absence of random-label fitting in these linear models. No verdict follows from positive surrogate loss alone, and the paper's solver difficulties at vanishing regularization do not test V2's comparison with true-label training.

versions.untested_parts: Standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods; test error at chance; unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
